$comment: How much public code still points at Microsoft 365 SMTP, measured
This exists because nobody has the number. Every article about the
December 2026 Basic auth shutdown says 'many systems will be affected'.
That is not a fact, it is a shrug. GitHub code search can put a floor
under it, and a weekly series shows whether the world is actually
WHAT THE NUMBER IS: public files, indexed by GitHub code search, that
WHAT IT IS NOT: a count of systems that will break. The same file may
be a live deployment, a template, a tutorial, or a fork of one of
those. Overstating it would make the figure easy to dismiss, which
defeats the point of measuring it.
Counts are what GitHub reports, and GitHub's totals are approximate.
A query that times out is recorded as null, never as zero - a failed
measurement that looks like a real drop would poison the series.

queries.label: smtp.office365.com
queries.note: The commercial Microsoft 365 SMTP endpoint. `NOT example` is doing two jobs: the bare phrase returns so many matches that GitHub's search API times out counting them, and excluding 'example' drops a large share of tutorials and placeholder templates. The remainder skews towards real configuration.

queries.label: smtp-mail.outlook.com
queries.note: The consumer Outlook.com endpoint, widely used by small deployments, hobby projects and devices set up with a personal account.
